content: Hi how can i assist you today
My smartwatch marks ‘high stress’ the moment I think about a tough conversation. It feels like it reads my mind.
Stress flags often rely on heart-rate variability and motion. What did the watch show right then—HR spike, HRV drop, or a generic alert?
It showed a red bar and a brief heart rate jump, no steps logged.
That combination can occur while seated. Were there any notifications or caffeine around that time that might align with the spike?
An email popped and I’d had coffee fifteen minutes earlier.
Those are common contributors. Do you see similar red bars during quiet periods without alerts or caffeine?
Rarely; the graph is flatter at night.
Night-time stability suggests fewer triggers. Do daytime spikes cluster around alerts, meetings, or specific hours?
Mostly near 10 a.m. stand reminders and after lunch.
That pattern points to routine moments. If a spike arrives with no surrounding events, noting what else was happening can make the picture clearer.
I’ll keep an eye on what coincides with it next time.
